_meta.description: Open-questions register: what is known, what is not, and how to discover the missing information — before decisions are made on the items below. Q-01…Q-50 numbering is carried from the prior register (S-PRIOR4) where the question predates this project; Q-Pxx are new here.
_meta.last_change: 2026-11-20 (arena/e1dbef32-prod2): Q-P19..Q-P22 appended — the manual-sourcing gap that blocks four planned guides, the cadence-resourcing question the new gate exposed, the FAQ framing decision, and the archived-build exposure. Each names the cheapest route to its answer. Append-only. | ids for this pass start after main's F-P29/Q-P18/SG-48/D-P23, which this register also carries — no row renumbered, no row dropped.

questions.question: Is the Associates account enrolled under tracking ID shopnow047c-20, and has each published link been validated in that account?
questions.known: The owner supplied shopnow047c-20 (brief, 2026-11-19). The format matches the documented US Store ID pattern (S-TAG). All five supplied short links resolved without a tag= (F-03). The site now publishes tagged Special Links built from verified ASINs. Whether the ID is registered and active is not observable from outside Associates Central.
questions.unknown: Account enrollment status; Partner Tag registration; whether test clicks report.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner logs into Associates Central: confirm the Partner Tag, generate or validate one Special Link per product, run a test click and read it in the report (protocol on the measurement page).

questions.question: Is the site's own trade name cleared, and does it contain an Amazon Mark?
questions.known: No Amazon Mark appears in any page title, meta description or target keyword (tools/checks.py fails the build if one does). The current wordmark is the project's established name 'Prod2' (D-P03), served under a github.io subpath — the site has no domain of its own yet.
questions.unknown: Whether a consumer-facing name (candidates in SG-01) collides with an existing trademark.
questions.how_to_discover: Re-read the Trademark Guidelines (S-POL) for domain and site names; run any candidate name through a trademark search before registering a domain.
questions.answerable_by: The owner, with a trademark search.

questions.question: Where can the self-hosted analytics endpoint run?
questions.known: server.mjs is dependency-free Node, counts events only (no IPs, no cookies, no referrers), and is ready to deploy. GitHub Pages cannot host it. Until a host exists, settings.analytics_endpoint stays empty and the site sends nothing.
questions.unknown: Which host the owner wants (any VM/container/Function that speaks HTTPS).
questions.how_to_discover: Owner picks a host; run the server; set the endpoint in data/p2/settings.json; rebuild. See the measurement page for the event contract.

questions.question: May the site publish prices and ratings under a dated-snapshot rule?
questions.known: Prices/ratings are currently withheld (F-02). D-19 already allows popularity claims as dated snapshots of official pages; extending that discipline to prices is an owner decision because it adds a re-verification obligation to every published page.
questions.unknown: Whether the owner wants the upkeep.
questions.how_to_discover: Decide SG-05; if yes, the checks must enforce 'price + read date' pairing.

questions.question: What is P2's exact preset/function count (24 or 25)?
questions.known: The title read 2026-11-19 says '24 One-Touch Preset Options'. Prior reads saw '24 cooking functions' and one section counting 25.
questions.unknown: The count as the manufacturer defines it.
questions.how_to_discover: Dated re-read of the listing's full spec/overview sections, or the manufacturer's product page.

questions.question: May the site ask readers for an email address, and what consent text would that need?
questions.known: The RSS feed captures readers without collecting personal data. Participation Requirement 6(g) bars rewarding clicks, so any list must stay clear of the affiliate links.
questions.unknown: Whether a list is wanted at all, and what the consent/privacy text should say.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner decision (SG-04); if yes, get the consent and privacy text reviewed before the first form ships.
questions.answerable_by: The owner, with a privacy reviewer.

questions.question: Which five events should the campaign ledger track?
questions.known: Resolved by adoption: the ledger's five defined events are impression, click, session, order, refund, each with the official attribution window from the Commission Income Statement (see measurement page). The site-side endpoint records five separate local events (page_view, outbound_click, guide_read_75, category_click, feed_click).
questions.unknown: Nothing — recorded so the definition is checkable (D-P05).
questions.how_to_discover: n/a

questions.question: Which question-shaped guide should be published next, and on what evidence of demand?
questions.known: The four brief-mandated guides plus two thermometer guides ship now (the accuracy guide and an instant-read vs leave-in workflow guide). Editorial hypotheses are working titles, not claims about search volume (D-19).
questions.unknown: Real query demand. No Search Console or analytics data exists yet (F-19).
questions.how_to_discover: After measurement is live: read first-party queries (Search Console + endpoint counts) for 4-6 weeks, then choose topics from measured queries (publishing cadence on the measurement page).

questions.question: Do the five submitted links continue to point at the same five products over time?
questions.known: On 2026-11-19 all five resolved to the recorded ASINs. Listings drift (titles change, variants swap, default offers change — F-44, F-49, F-29).
questions.unknown: Future drift.
questions.how_to_discover: Re-run the verification pass each season or before any campaign push; record dated observations in the register.

questions.question: Should the two thermometer products get their own buying guide cluster (seasonal grilling / holiday gift angle)?
questions.known: Thermometers are half the catalog; two thermometer guides now ship (accuracy, and an instant-read vs leave-in workflow guide). A full seasonal cluster is still an editorial and SEO investment, not a data problem.
questions.unknown: Owner appetite for the extra content.
questions.how_to_discover: Review SG-03 alongside measured queries (Q-P02).

questions.question: Is any product imagery usable on the site, and through which official channel?
questions.known: The Operating Agreement Section 1 treats images as Program Content. Generated or copied photography is not an option under this project's rules (S-18, D-22).
questions.unknown: Which Amazon-served or brand-supplied images the Associates terms allow for this use, and whether the owner has a licence path.
questions.how_to_discover: Read the imagery clauses of the Operating Agreement and Program Policies with the owner's Associates contact, or ask Associates support in writing. Until then the site stays text-led.
questions.answerable_by: The account holder, with Associates support.

questions.question: Does the owner control a domain for Search Console and the analytics endpoint?
questions.known: The site is served from the GitHub Pages address wingbangboozle1-lang.github.io/Prod2. Search Console verification and a hosted endpoint both need an owner-controlled HTTPS address (SG-06).
questions.unknown: Whether a custom domain exists or is wanted, and who holds Search Console access.
questions.how_to_discover: The owner checks the domain registrar and the Search Console account. If none exists, the Pages address can be verified as a URL-prefix property.

questions.question: Which seasonal window should the first thermometer cluster target?
questions.known: The two thermometer listings describe grill and BBQ use and gift angles in their titles. No dated search or sales data exists in this project, and none is claimed.
questions.unknown: Whether any seasonal demand is real for these products, and the timing of the next season.
questions.how_to_discover: Read Search Console queries for thermometer terms after SG-06. Do not use listing titles as evidence of demand.
questions.answerable_by: The owner, from Search Console data.

questions.question: Who verifies the site in Google Search Console, and when?
questions.known: The site ships with everything Search Console needs to index it well: one canonical URL per page, unique titles and meta descriptions, sitemap.xml, robots.txt with the Sitemap line, and an RSS feed. The build is ready for the verification token (settings.json -> search_console.verification_token).
questions.unknown: Which verification method the owner prefers (HTML tag, HTML file, or DNS), and when the property will be claimed.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner opens Search Console, adds the property https://wingbangboozle1-lang.github.io/Prod2/, chooses the HTML-tag method, pastes the token into settings.json and rebuilds (or uploads the HTML file). Then submits sitemap.xml and feed.xml. Step list is on the measurement page.
questions.answerable_by: The account holder (needs the owner's Google account).

questions.question: Which of the three specified design directions should the next visual pass implement?
questions.known: The carried brief (DESIGN_PROMPT.md) specifies Direction A, warm editorial, and this build follows it. Two alternative directions are fully specified in the suggestion queue (SG-31): a clean modern shop and a bold magazine layout, each with the same compliance block. No reader data exists to choose between them (Q-P05 open).
questions.unknown: The owner's preference, and whether any brand-name change (Q-19, SG-01) should ship in the same pass.
questions.how_to_discover: Review SG-31 side by side on the suggestions page and record the pick in the decision log; the token layer (SG-33) then makes the switch mechanical.
questions.answerable_by: The site owner (taste call); Search Console data can inform it later.

questions.question: Which event vocabulary should the site and the endpoint share?
questions.known: server.mjs accepts page_view, outbound_click, guide_open, category_open, rss_feed_click, chooser_completed, article_half_read, disclosure_viewed, cta_click, product_click, filter_apply and guide_read. The site emits five: page_view, outbound_click, guide_read_75, category_click, feed_click. Answered 2026-11-20 (arena/644d217b-prod2): the site's five documented events are the contract; the collector was extended to accept and correctly aggregate all five, and the gate now fails the build on any divergence. No event was invented or renamed to fit the collector.
questions.recommendation: Extend server.mjs to accept the three site events and map target_host. It is additive, it touches no browser code, and it preserves the instrumentation that is already tested. Then add a gate that reads both files and fails if the lists ever diverge again.
questions.unknown: A decision on which side moves. Extending the server keeps the site's already-shipped instrumentation and costs twelve lines of Node; changing measure.js keeps the server untouched but means editing and re-testing the only code that touches a reader's browser.
questions.how_to_discover: Compare the two lists against what the owner actually wants to know at launch. If the answer is 'how many people clicked a product', the site's five already cover it and the server should be extended. If the answer is 'which guides get read', the server's article_half_read/guide_read pair is richer and measure.js should adopt it.
questions.answer: Published vocabulary = the five in data/p2/events.json. Collector updated to match, gate enforces the match, regression test pins it. See D-P21.

questions.question: Does the owner ratify the working brand “The Crisp Counter”, and will a formal trade-name clearance be run?
questions.known: Adopted 2026-11-20 as the working wordmark on the owner's standing anti-slop directive (decision D-P18). A preliminary web search on 2026-11-20 returned no conflicting kitchen-appliance brand in the first page of results; the name comes from the adopted design brief (DESIGN_PROMPT.md).
questions.unknown: No formal trademark search has been performed (USPTO registry, state registries, common-law use, domain availability). The owner has not individually ratified the specific name.
questions.how_to_discover: Run the USPTO trademark search (tmsearch.uspto.gov) for 'Crisp Counter' word marks in class 7/11/35; check state registries and live web/common-law use; check domain availability (Q-P06); then record ratify-or-revert in the decision log.
questions.answerable_by: Owner (with counsel for the formal search)

questions.question: May the site publish availability snapshots (“observed in stock on YYYY-MM-DD”) alongside its dated listing reads?
questions.known: Answered 2026-11-20 by the policy read recorded in decision D-P11: Program Policies 2(b) (updated 2026-04-14, read 2026-11-20) permits prices and availability only when Amazon serves the link or the data comes via the Creators/PA API — a dated snapshot is neither. The site therefore publishes neither prices nor availability; both stay blank with a link to the live listing (F-02 posture).
questions.unknown: Nothing remains for this session to discover; the policy question is recorded. Revisit only if Amazon grants Creators/PA API access (then D-21 applies).
questions.how_to_discover: If PA API access is granted later, pull availability (and prices/ratings) through the API per the Operating Agreement; otherwise no discovery path exists inside policy.

questions.question: How long should a piece be before it is published, and how is that enforced?
questions.known: The ten original guides run 436-814 words. The two long reads added 2026-11-20 run 1,212-1,295 words. There is no stated minimum in any register, and the gate does not measure length, so 'thin' is currently a judgement call rather than a check.
questions.unknown: Whether a length floor is the right control at all; word count is a weak proxy for usefulness and a strong invitation to pad.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner picks one of: (a) no floor, judged per piece; (b) a floor of ~600 words for a guide and ~1,000 for a long read, gated; (c) a sourced-claims-per-100-words floor, which measures substance rather than length. Option (c) is the only one that cannot be satisfied by filler.
blocks: Any scaling of the content set

questions.question: Can this project show the real product photo at all, and through which channel?
questions.known: Every card carries a generated illustration with the line 'Illustration, not the product photo'. The Operating Agreement and IP License restrict use of Program Content including images, and this project has no Creators/PA API access.
questions.unknown: Whether Associates enrollees can obtain product images through the Associates Central link builder without API approval; whether an approved application would be granted for a site this size. Not verifiable from outside the account.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner checks Associates Central for the SiteStripe image/link tool on one enrolled product and reports whether an image can be obtained with a compliant attribution. That single test settles it.
blocks: The shelf looking like a real shop

questions.question: Where will the analytics endpoint actually run, and who pays for it?
questions.known: server.mjs is written, tested (3/3) and now accepts every event the site sends. settings.analytics_endpoint is empty, so the site transmits nothing and counts only in each visitor's own browser.
questions.unknown: Host choice, cost, and whether the owner wants to run a Node service at all. Also unknown: retention period and who reads the aggregate.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner names a host, or decides the browser-local counter is enough for now. If the latter, the measurement page must say so plainly rather than implying traffic data exists.
blocks: Every claim that the site is measured

questions.question: Is there an official, quotable source for how these specific machines behave — holding temperature, reheat settings, preheat, clearance — or does the site stop at the specification sheet?
questions.known: The three air-fryer listings read by this site state capacity, dimensions, controls and feature sets. None of the reads on record states a keep-warm holding temperature, a reheat instruction or a preheat requirement. The USDA FSIS hot-holding list names chafing dishes, steam tables, warming trays and slow cookers — not air fryers — and the peer-reviewed extension handout tells readers to 'check out the operator's manual to learn more about how the air fryer works' rather than answering it itself.
questions.unknown: Whether the manufacturers' manuals state a holding temperature or a reheating instruction for these models; whether this site may quote them; whether anyone can source 'preheat' either way. Until then the answer to 'can this air fryer hold food at 140°F' is 'unverified', and four planned guides cannot be written honestly.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner-supplied route (cheapest first): (1) read the official product manual for each of P1/P2/P3 from the manufacturer's support page and record it in data/p2/sources.json with its date; (2) if the manual is silent, record the silence, which is itself publishable and closes the question; (3) real measurements — a probe in a held dish — would answer it outright, and the leave-in probe on the shelf is the tool for it.
questions.answerable_by: Owner (documents and, optionally, a measurement); no external party can answer it for these three models.
blocks: Queue slots 1 and 3 (preheat rituals, second functions)
Any how-to-use claim on the shop pages

questions.question: Is a 14-day publishing rhythm resourced — and what happens to the slots that are not answerable yet?
questions.known: The register declares a 14-day cadence and the nine queued slots are spaced exactly 14 days apart (measured 2026-11-20), so the schedule is internally consistent. The gate now keeps it honest: shipping without advancing next_due_utc fails the build (F-P35, resolved), which is why next_due reads 2026-12-04 after today's three pages. Slot 1 is marked blocked, not overdue, because its stated source cannot answer its question (Q-P19).
questions.unknown: Who writes, at what rate, with what review. Nothing in this repository records the owner's available time or an author, and no assumption about either has been invented here. Also unknown: whether the owner wants blocked slots re-ordered ahead of scheduled ones when a manual arrives.
questions.how_to_discover: One line from the owner: a number and a source of authors. If the answer is 'no reliable rhythm', delete the fortnightly promise from index.html and guides.html and set the cadence line to what is true — the gate will enforce whatever is written, and stays silent if the promise is removed.
blocks: F-P35's successor: any public cadence claim

questions.question: Now that FAQ blocks exist mechanically, should they be retro-fitted to the other guides — and does the site describe them as a search tactic or as reader structure?
questions.known: Two new guides carry visible question-and-answer blocks, and the build derives matching FAQPage markup only from those blocks; the gate fails if the two lists diverge. Google's own guidance as read 2026-11-20 says the FAQ rich result was narrowed to well-known authoritative government and health sites in August 2023, that its changelog records removal of the FAQ rich-result documentation in June 2026, and that its supported-features gallery no longer lists FAQ.
questions.unknown: Whether the owner wants the markup on every guide for machine readability and answer extraction (a real but unmeasured benefit), or wants it nowhere as an SEO gesture. Also unknown: whether the ten older guides have questions worth surfacing, which is an editorial judgement, not a technical one.
questions.how_to_discover: Decide the framing first (reader structure, not SERP trick); then, if yes, add a genuine Q&A pair per existing guide from material already on the page — the gate then enforces the pairing, so no page can claim an FAQ it does not show.
blocks: Any claim that this site optimises for FAQ rich results

questions.question: Do the archived builds stay in the published branch, or does the Pages source change make the question moot?
questions.known: site/ (25 files) and archive/countertop-dispatch/ are tracked at the repository root; while the Pages source is the root (F-P19) they are reachable by URL, with their own titles and no canonical pointing at the live site. The generated robots.txt now asks crawlers to stay out of both, which is a request, not a control.
questions.unknown: Whether the owner will flip Pages to the workflow artifact (which serves docs/ only and removes the exposure completely) or prefers to keep the archive reachable on purpose — a legitimate choice for a project that publishes its own receipts.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner action on F-P19 (Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions), or an explicit 'keep it reachable' decision, recorded as a decision row so the next session does not re-litigate it.
